title: PMSV FSSAI Advertising & Claims Rule Core

source_policy.fail_closed_rule: If the claim condition depends on a nutrient, comparator, laboratory result, process history, scientific substantiation or product classification that PMSV cannot verify deterministically, the claim is returned as NEEDS EVIDENCE rather than approved.

current_source.authority: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
current_source.regulation: Food Safety and Standards (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018

general_principles.text: Claims must be truthful, unambiguous, meaningful, not misleading and help consumers comprehend the information.
Claims shall not encourage or condone excess consumption of a particular food.
Claims shall not suggest that a balanced and varied diet cannot provide appropriate quantities of nutrients.
Where the claimed benefit depends on preparation, the relevant preparation method must be provided on the label.
Reduction-of-disease-risk claims must specify the number of servings per day for the claimed benefit.
Nutritional or health attributes must be scientifically substantiated using validated methods for the ingredient or substance that is the basis of the claim.
Potentially misleading brand/fancy names using words such as natural, fresh, pure, original, traditional, authentic, genuine or real require the prescribed front-of-pack disclaimer.
FSSAI logo or licence number shall not be used to make or promote a claim.
Advertisements shall not undermine the importance of healthy lifestyles.
Food or beverage advertisements shall not portray the product as a meal replacement unless specifically permitted.
Claims in advertisements must be consistent with information on the label.
No deceptive advertisement shall be made.

conditions: No sugars of any type are added.
No ingredient containing sugars as an ingredient is used.
No ingredient containing sugars that substitutes for added sugars is used.
The sugar content is not increased by other means such as enzymatic starch hydrolysis.
sugars.screening_note: A direct match fails the no-added-sugars screen. No match does not approve the claim because compound ingredients and process-generated sugars still require evidence.

conditions: No sodium salts are added.
No ingredient containing added sodium salts is used.
No ingredient containing sodium salts that substitutes for added salt is used.
sodium_salts.screening_note: A direct match fails the no-added-salt screen. No match does not approve the claim because sodium salts in compound ingredients or substitutes still require evidence.

conditions: The additive or functional class has not been added or removed at manufacture.
It is not contained in any ingredient except where naturally present.
It is an additive permitted for that product.
It has not been replaced by another additive giving equivalent characteristics.
additives.direct_runtime_rule: Use PMSV ingredient qualification: any ingredient classified as an active food additive is a direct disqualifier for a broad 'no additives' claim. Compound ingredients remain a manual evidence gate.

prohibited_claims.text: No claim may refer to suitability for prevention, alleviation, treatment or cure of a disease, disorder or physiological condition unless specifically permitted under another FSSAI regulation.
Labels shall not state or imply recommendation, prescription or approval by medical, nutrition or health professionals or for medical purpose.
The term 'added nutrients' shall not be claimed when nutrients were added merely to compensate nutrients lost or removed during processing.
Claims that create doubt or suspicion about the safety of similar food or arouse fear are prohibited.
No health claim shall be made for food containing nutrients or constituents in quantities that increase disease or adverse-health risk.
Advertisements or claims shall not undermine another manufacturer's products to promote the advertiser's product.

schedule_i.note: Schedule I specifies the 4 kcal threshold for liquids; PMSV does not invent a solid threshold.
Depends on current RDA percentage under Schedule I; PMSV does not auto-approve until a current official RDA denominator is linked.

schedule_i.condition: ≥10^8 CFU in recommended serving size per day
GI below 55 using the prescribed test definition/reference foods
At least 40 mg DHA per 100 g or per 100 kcal

claims.relationship: Calcium or calcium + Vitamin D and osteoporosis
conditions: Food is a source/high in calcium or calcium + vitamin D.
Beneficial effect linked to daily recommended intake.
Food is low in sodium at the Schedule III threshold.
Claim context states benefit is obtained with a low-sodium diet.

claims.relationship: Dietary saturated fat and blood cholesterol
conditions: Food meets low-saturated-fat condition.
Claim context states benefit is obtained with a diet low in fat/saturated fat and physical activity.

claims.relationship: Potassium and risk of high blood pressure
conditions: Food is a good source of potassium.
Food is low in sodium.
Food is low in total fat and saturated fat.
At least 1 g omega-3 fatty acids per 100 g, 100 ml or 100 kcal.
Claim context states beneficial effect with daily intake of 2 g ALA.

claims.relationship: Soluble dietary fibre and blood cholesterol
conditions: Applicable soluble fibre source such as oats/barley/millets.
At least 1 g soluble dietary fibre per serving.
Claim context states beneficial effect with daily intake of 3 g soluble dietary fibre.
At least 1 g plant sterols/stanols per serving.
Claim context states beneficial effect with daily intake up to 3 g/day.
Food is oats or barley.
At least 4 g beta-glucans per 30 g available carbohydrate in the quantified portion.
Claim states it is taken as part of a meal.

schedule_iii.prior_approval_note: Reduction-of-disease-risk claims outside claims defined with criteria under these or other FSSAI regulations require prior Food Authority approval under Regulation 11.

claims.claim: Vitamin A helps against night blindness.
Vitamin B12 is important for normal nervous-system function and blood formation.
Folate and folic acid are important for blood formation.
Iodine is required for normal growth and thyroid and brain function.
Zinc supports a healthy immune system.
Thiamine is required for normal nerve and heart function.
Riboflavin is necessary to release energy from food.
Niacin is necessary to release energy from food.
Pyridoxine is necessary to release energy from food.

schedule_iv.eligibility_note: These claims apply to food articles fortified in accordance with the Food Safety and Standards (Fortification of Foods) Regulations, 2018.

schedule_v.summary: Restricted to qualifying single foods or qualifying natural ingredients/additives; composite foods may use 'made from natural ingredients' only when all ingredients/additives qualify. 'Natural goodness', 'naturally better' and 'nature's way' shall not be used.

evidence_questions.question: Is the finished product a single food (not a composite food)?
Has nothing been added to that single food?
Has it undergone only the processing permitted by Schedule V for 'Natural'?
Where packaging applies, is it done without chemicals and preservatives as required by Schedule V?

schedule_v.summary: Restricted to products not processed beyond the permitted minimal processes; special conditions apply to frozen-from-fresh expressions.

evidence_questions.question: Has the product avoided processing other than the Schedule V permitted minimal/safety processes?
Have those processes not altered the product's basic characteristics?

schedule_v.summary: Restricted to qualifying single-ingredient food with nothing added and compliant contaminant levels; compound foods may use 'made with pure ingredients' only when all ingredients qualify.

evidence_questions.question: Is the food free from avoidable contamination?
Are unavoidable contaminants below the applicable FSSAI limits?

schedule_v.summary: Use requires clarification of the tangible quality justification and why the term is used.

evidence_questions.question: Does the label/advertisement clearly state the tangible quality justification for using this term?
Does it clearly explain why this particular term is used?

schedule_v.summary: Recipe, fundamental formulation or process must demonstrably have existed substantially unchanged for a generation (30 years).

evidence_questions.question: Can the recipe, fundamental formulation or processing method be demonstrated to have existed for at least 30 years?
Has it remained substantially unchanged for that same period?

schedule_v.summary: Origin of formulation/process must be traceable and essentially unchanged; major ingredients cannot be replaced and the product must remain the standard product when variants are introduced.

evidence_questions.question: Can the origin of the formulation or process be traced?
Has it remained essentially unchanged over time?
Does it contain no replacements for major ingredients?
When newer variants exist, does this remain available as the standard product?

prior_approval.text: Prior Food Authority approval is required for reduction-of-disease-risk claims other than those defined with criteria under these or other FSSAI regulations.

required_information: Ingredient, nutrient or substance on which the claim is based.
Validated analytical method for the ingredient or substance.
Explanation of how the claim is clear, meaningful and comprehensible to consumers.
Well-designed human intervention studies for health claims conducted by or under guidance of established research institutions.

non_compliance.text: Advertisements or claims not complying with the regulation are subject to penalty under section 53 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

redress.text: Misleading claims may be referred to or taken up by the Food Authority, which may seek clarification, decide acceptance/rejection and suggest improvement.

corrective_advertisement.text: Where an advertisement violates the regulation, the Food Authority may require it to stop immediately and require a corrective advertisement through the same medium.
